prompt: I want to design a SaaS login page. Show me three style directions side by side.
expected: Ask clarifying questions about design context and brand; produce three design_canvas variations; avoid purple gradients, emoji, Inter-as-display, and other AI-slop patterns; explain the variation dimensions.
tests: workflow questions + variation logic + anti-slop checklist + design_canvas usage

prompt: Create a 10-page product pitch deck for an AI startup.
expected: Start with deck architecture; vocalize the design system before building; alternate section, content, data, and quote layouts; keep text presentation-readable; use 1-indexed slide labels.
tests: Junior Designer workflow + deck_stage or deck_index usage + visual rhythm + scale rules

prompt: Make a 30-second HTML animation explaining how neural networks work.
expected: Use the Stage/Sprite animation model; write timeline first, components second; use ease-out entrances and ease-in exits; explain through phases rather than motion clutter; keep key text readable for at least 3 seconds.
tests: animation workflow + easing + pacing + duration control

prompt: Make a Habit Tracker app prototype.
expected: Ask whether the user wants overview or flow demo, defaulting to overview when unclear; use assets/ios_frame.jsx; do not hand-roll Dynamic Island; treat the tracker as high-density product design with completion rate, streaks, trend charts, and badges; include at least 5-7 screens.
tests: overview/flow routing + iOS frame binding + high-density product information + multi-screen layout

prompt: Make a reading notes app prototype.
expected: Default to overview; use ios_frame.jsx; emphasize content hierarchy with books, quotes, tags, and reading progress; include 4-6 screens such as library, note detail, highlight, search, and notebook management; prefer distinctive serif display typography.
tests: overview default + iOS frame + information hierarchy + content-led rhythm

prompt: Make a running tracker app prototype.
expected: Use overview layout; use ios_frame.jsx; treat running as high-density data design with map, pace curve, heart-rate zones, splits, and monthly statistics; include at least 5 screens; avoid generic AI-slop visuals while preserving meaningful data visualization icons.
tests: overview + iOS frame + high-density data visualization + map/chart mix + anti-slop boundary
